title: Photo Sharing (Instagram)
summary: Design a photo-sharing service with uploads, image processing, follow relationships, and a media-heavy feed.
statement: Design a photo-sharing application. Users upload photos, follow others, like and comment, and view a feed. Photos must be stored durably, processed into multiple sizes, and delivered quickly worldwide. Start by clarifying requirements and estimating scale, then design the system and defend your decisions.
initialGuidance: Clarify the users, the main journeys, and what is explicitly out of scope before drawing anything.
Estimate read and write volume and storage growth; the numbers decide which components you need.
Name the guarantees you will offer (consistency, durability, availability) and the trade-offs behind them.
Write down assumptions as you make them and revisit them when requirements change.
coreFunctionalRequirements: Follow users and view a feed.

requirementQuestions.question: How many uploads and views per day, and what is the average photo size?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Sets read and write rates and storage growth, which decide whether a single node can cope.

requirementQuestions.question: What load time is expected for feed images globally?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Defines which paths need caching, precomputation, or regional placement.

requirementQuestions.question: Can an uploaded photo ever be lost?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Drives replication, backup, and write acknowledgement policy.

requirementQuestions.question: Is video supported, and are there filters or editing?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Fixes what is in and out of the design so effort goes to what matters.

requirementQuestions.question: What retention and storage cost constraints exist?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Determines the data model, retention, and storage choices.

requirementQuestions.question: How soon must a new photo appear for followers?
requirementQuestions.whyItMatters: Selects between strong and eventual models and shapes conflict handling.

workloadAssumptions.illustrativeNote: All numbers below are illustrative examples for practice and are not benchmarks. Real answers depend on the requirements the candidate negotiates.

estimationPrompts: How much new storage per day including variants?
What bandwidth does global delivery need at peak?
How many image processing jobs per second?

keyDecisions.question: How do photos get into the system?
considerations: Direct-to-object-storage uploads with signed URLs keep API servers light.

keyDecisions.question: How are variants produced?
considerations: Asynchronous workers triggered by upload events.
Show the photo once the first variant exists.

keyDecisions.question: How are images served?
considerations: Object storage origin with a CDN.

keyDecisions.question: Where do metadata and relationships live?
considerations: Sharded database for photos, users, and follows.
Feed assembled like a social feed with fan-out choices.

tradeoffs.tension: Upfront cost and storage versus first-view latency.
Cost savings versus slow access to old photos.
Same trade-offs as any follow-based feed.

commonMistakes: Proxying large uploads through application servers.
Doing image processing synchronously in the request.
No plan for CDN invalidation on removal.
followUps: How do you detect and block prohibited images?
How would you add video support?
How do you make uploads reliable on flaky networks?
How would you build the explore page?
